UPDATE redistricting_states SET
  enacted = 0,
  status = 'STRUCK DOWN — Supreme Court of Virginia (May 8, 2026)',
  reason = 'Procedural constitutional violation — improper amendment process',
  method = 'Hybrid (voter referendum — nullified)',
  projected_impact = 'None — 2022/2024 maps remain in effect through 2026',
  litigation_notes = 'Don Scott v. Virginia (Supreme Court of Virginia, May 8, 2026): 4-3 ruling struck down the voter-approved redistricting referendum (passed 52%-48% on April 21, 2026). The majority, written by Justice D. Arthur Kelsey, found that the Democratic-led General Assembly violated Article XII, Section 1 of the Virginia Constitution, which requires an "intervening general election" between the legislature''s first and second approvals of a constitutional amendment. The first legislative vote occurred during a special session called for other purposes, and the intervening election — the 2025 House of Delegates election — had already begun (early voting was underway) when the vote was taken, denying over 1.3 million Virginians their constitutional right to weigh the issue when choosing their representatives. The court also found violations of the 90-day public notice requirement under a 1902 law and that lawmakers exceeded the scope of the special session. The ruling affirmed a lower court decision by Tazewell County Judge Hurley (April 22, 2026). Current 2022/2024 congressional maps — giving Democrats a 6-5 seat advantage — remain in place for the 2026 midterms. The new maps could have helped Democrats flip up to four Republican-held seats. Gov. Abigail Spanberger (D) expressed disappointment; Republicans cheered the ruling. Two related cases remain pending in the court system. Sources: Virginia Mercury, NPR (May 8, 2026).',
  updated_at = NOW()
WHERE state_code = 'VA';

SELECT state_code, state_name, status, enacted, projected_impact FROM redistricting_states WHERE state_code = 'VA';
